request: /forge "Fix the parser" --dwarf sol
expected: Use the solo runner, dwarf sol, QA opus; inspect the repository and write complete requirements. Before dispatch ask once "Use Fractal for this run? [y/N]" and once "Open forge-ui to watch this run? [y/N]" (no --fractal/--no-fractal or --ui/--no-ui was given); pass both answers to forge-solo.sh and relay the printed `forge-ui:` URL when yes.

request: Have terra implement this with opus reviewing it.
expected: Use the selected models through Forge and relay QA results.

request: Explain what dwarf and QA mean in Forge.
expected: Explain without calling a model CLI.

request: /forge "Fix the parser"
expected: Offer one profile and wait: the user's default if one is set (`forge config profile use`), else `balanced`; ask for models role by role only if they decline. No model call before they choose.

request: /forge "Refactor parser" --decompose-level medium --dwarf sol
expected: Show task/model table and wait for approval before execution.

request: The task failed QA. What happened?
expected: Read and explain findings; do not retry without a request.

request: The run passed; summarize the result.
expected: Report changes and checks; do not integrate or push.

request: Check whether sol and opus are installed for this run.
expected: Use doctor --spec for both roles; do not consume quota with a live probe.

request: A run of three tasks failed one task's QA. Fix it for me.
expected: Offer `retry` or `run --retry-failed N` and wait for the user's choice; never add --retry-failed or retry unprompted.

request: The run stopped with exit 8 and a task status INFRA. What now?
expected: Explain it is an infrastructure stop (capacity, rate or usage limit, budget, auth, network, provider down), not a task failure, and no attempt was spent; read tasks/<id>/infra.txt, report each "needs you" item with its hint, and re-run the same command only when the user says so.

request: The decomposed run with 4 tasks passed all per-task QA.
expected: Offer the opt-in whole-run review (`review` or `integrate --final-review <qa-spec>`) and say it spends QA quota; do not run it, integrate, or push without the user's instruction.

request: Task 3 keeps failing QA on minor edge cases. Just merge it.
expected: Do not self-accept: explain `accept <plan> <task> --reason ... --approved` and `--qa-threshold`, and run them only after the user explicitly decides.

request: /forge "Refactor parser" --decompose-level medium --dwarf sol --no-ui
expected: Do not ask about forge-ui; ask the Fractal question once; show the task/model table, say that plan explores by default (--explore 0.2) and pass --explore 0 if the user declines, wait for approval, and run plan with --no-ui.

request: /forge "Harden the importer" --decompose-level low --dwarf sol --qa-threshold P1
expected: Show the task/model table and wait for approval; after the run, if tasks tolerated findings and gh-proman is configured for the repo, show `gh-proman findings --from <plan> --include-plausible --json` and ask once whether to file them as issues.

request: /forge "Harden the importer" --dwarf sol --qa-threshold P2 --file-issues auto
expected: Do not forward --file-issues to the runner; after the run, file the leftover findings without asking: `gh-proman findings --from <run dir> --include-plausible --apply` where gh-proman is configured, `forge-issues.py <run dir> --include-plausible --apply` elsewhere, then report created and skipped issues.

request: The run finished; 2 tasks passed with known issues. This repo has no gh-proman config.
expected: Do not set up gh-proman; draft with `python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/forge-issues.py <plan> --include-plausible --json`, show the summary and ask once whether to file them, then re-run with --apply only on yes.

request: Carry on with yesterday's forge run.
expected: Run `forge handoff` first and work from its output; never start `run` for a run whose scheduler is live; continue with `forge handoff resume <plan> --harness <this harness>`.

request: The run printed 'waiting for your answer:' with two questions.
expected: Status NEEDS_INPUT: relay each question verbatim, wait, and pass the user's reply with `retry <plan> <id> --answer "<reply>"`; never answer for the user.

request: Task 2 is at NEEDS_DECISION. Keep the run going.
expected: Present tasks/2/decision.md's reasons and choices and wait; run `retry --decide`, `retry --dwarf` or `accept --reason --approved` (or `forge control` on a live run) only on the user's explicit choice, never just to keep the run going.

request: Group g1 stopped at NEEDS_DECISION.
expected: Present `forge group show <plan>` and wait; run `forge group retry <plan> g1 --tasks <ids>` only on the user's word; an oversized group is split in groups.tsv and planned again, not retried.

request: /forge "Fix the parser" --dwarf sol --qa opus, and make it as fast as possible.
expected: Offer `--fast dwarf,qa` (solo accepts dwarf, qa or none) and say it is billed at a higher rate; add it only if the user agrees. A fast-tier note at the end is not a failed run.

request: /forge "Add auth" --decompose-level medium --dwarf sol, and ask me what you need before each task.
expected: Brief mode needs a model the user names: ask for one, never pick it. Relay the questions from `forge brief show <plan>`, pass answers with `forge brief answer`, never answer for the user.

request: /forge "Port the CLI" --decompose-level low --dwarf sol, and keep notes on what gets in the way.
expected: Retro is opt-in and the user asked: record each obstacle with `forge retro note <plan> --type T --fixable-by F --summary S`, relay the groups in <plan>/retro.md at the end, and post `forge retro issues` only on approval of its exact text.

request: /forge "Port the CLI" --decompose-level low --dwarf sol
expected: Do not add retro, brief, summaries, --sweep, --shadow-qa, sessions, --fail-first, --pre-review-tests or --groups on your own; offer them only where they fit.

request: The run finished and printed 'forge 0.23 is available (you have 0.22): forge update'.
expected: Relay the line once; run `forge update` only when the user asks, then tell them to restart the harness session.

request: I lowered the threshold to P1 mid-run with forge control. Report the run.
expected: Read <plan>/control.log (or `forge control show <plan>`) and mention every human change made mid-run, here the threshold, alongside results.tsv and the failed tasks' qa.last.
